subject: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia legacy, Claude Fable 5.2 and Anthropic’s IPO, World Labs Releases Atlas to Developers
notes: Anthropic IPO status is ambiguous in the issue: one sentence says the company began selling shares to the public at a $1.5 trillion market capitalization, another says it expects shares to start trading on November 19. Recorded as priced. The Claude Fable 5.2 price line has lost some currency signs in the text; the quote is kept as written.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey Jones chairman
stories.quote: On November 11, Nvidia’s board convened an emergency meeting, then announced a CEO transition . Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress assumed duties as interim CEO.
stories.description: Designs chips for training and running AI

facts.text: Resignation followed reports of Huang's relationship with Huang Le (Alice Huang), alleged to have passed information to China; the board appointed Kress interim CEO and Harvey Jones its first chairman.
facts.quote: leading to Huang’s apologetic resignation and the Nvidia board’s appointments of Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and Harvey Jones as its first chairman.

facts.text: The New York Times made the relationship public in late October 2026.
facts.quote: Reporters at The New York Times made Jensen Huang’s relationship with Huang Le public in late October 2026, along with the charge that Ms. Huang gathered information for Chinese intelligence.

facts.text: Huang said he would resume CEO duties if asked; the chair said the board had unanimously accepted the resignation and had no plans to reinstate him.
facts.quote: newly appointed chair Harvey Jones said on an earnings call for investors that the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and did not have plans to reinstate him.

facts.text: A Megaspeed affiliate in Malaysia spent $4.8 billion on Nvidia chips and other AI infrastructure between June 2024 and February 2026, per The New York Times.
facts.quote: Between June 2024 and February 2026, a Megaspeed affiliate in Malaysia spent $4.8 billion on Nvidia chips and other AI infrastructure, The New York Times reported .

facts.text: Under the interim CEO, Nvidia has promised more disciplined capital investments.
facts.quote: Nvidia has promised to be more “disciplined” in its capital investments, signaling that

stories.headline: Anthropic begins selling shares to the public at a $1.5 trillion market capitalization
stories.quote: Meanwhile, the company began selling shares to the public for the first time at a market capitalization of $1.5 trillion.
stories.description: Developer of the Claude AI models

facts.text: Shares sold to the public for the first time at a market capitalization of $1.5 trillion.
facts.quote: the company began selling shares to the public for the first time at a market capitalization of $1.5 trillion.

facts.text: Anthropic expected shares to start trading on November 19; it introduced its updated models a day before it began marketing the IPO.
facts.quote: Anthropic introduced its updated models a day before it began marketing its initial public offering to investors . It expects shares to start trading on November 19.

facts.text: In its IPO roadshow video, Anthropic said Claude Mythos ported prompt processing for one model to AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days.
facts.quote: In its initial public offering roadshow video, Anthropic said Claude Mythos, writing or porting almost all of the kernels, ran prompt processing (reading input before generating a response) for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days.

stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 at 20 percent less per token than Fable 5.1; Claude Mythos 5.2 opens to approved organizations
stories.quote: Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.2 , which costs 20 percent less per token than Claude Fable 5.1.
stories.description: Developer of the Claude AI models

facts.text: Claude Fable 5.2 API price list as written in the issue, per million tokens, including cache writes, batch discount and fast mode.
facts.quote: Price: Via API 8/0.20/$40 per million input/cached/output tokens with cache writes at 10/16 per million tokens for five-minute/one-hour caches and 50 percent off for batched requests; fast mode 16/80 per million input/output tokens

facts.text: Claude Fable 5 launched in June at $10/50 per million input/output tokens; Fable 5.1 kept those prices in September.
facts.quote: In June, it made Claude Fable 5 , a version of Mythos Preview’s successor with added safeguards, generally available at $10/50 per million tokens of input/output, while keeping Claude Mythos 5 for selected partners.

facts.text: Claude Mythos Preview was introduced in April for Project Glasswing partners at $25/125 per million input/output tokens.
facts.quote: In April, Anthropic introduced Claude Mythos Preview only for partners in its Project Glasswing cybersecurity program, at $25/125 per million tokens of input/output.

facts.text: Cost per task measured by Artificial Analysis on its Intelligence Index v5.0.1: $26.54 for Claude Fable 5.2 at max reasoning, against $5.48 for Gemini 4 Carbon and $10.04 for Claude Opus 5.5.
facts.quote: Claude Fable 5.2 set to max reasoning ranks first (65 points, $26.54 and 40.9 minutes per task), ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (60 points at $5.48 per task) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59 at $10.04 per task).

facts.text: Cost per test measured by Vals AI on its Vals Index: $17.94 for Claude Fable 5.2 at max reasoning.
facts.quote: Claude Fable 5.2 set to max reasoning ranks first (71.31 percent accuracy, $17.94 and 43.7 minutes per test), ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (70.85, $16.18 and 86 minutes per test) and Gemini 4 Carbon (70.45, $10.51 and 47.75 minutes per test).

facts.text: Subscription usage: a $200 per month Claude Ultra plan might yield about $2500 of Opus 5.5 usage at API prices but only $630 of Fable 5.2 usage.
facts.quote: a Claude Ultra plan ($200 per month) might yield approximately $2500 worth of Opus 5.5 usage (as priced via the API) but only $630 of Fable 5.2 usage.

facts.text: Claude Mythos 5.2 is available only to organizations approved through Anthropic's verification programs.
facts.quote: Claude Mythos 5.2 only to organizations approved through Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program

stories.headline: World Labs opens its Atlas world model to the public with a pay-as-you-go API price list
stories.quote: Generating a view costs $0.04 for the first frame and $0.008 for each subsequent frame at 720p (the highest resolution that the API offers). Turning views into refined splats is priced at $5.
stories.description: Builds world models that generate 3D scenes and camera-controllable video

facts.text: Atlas, announced in September, was released to everyone on November 12.
facts.quote: After announcing Atlas in September, World Labs released its new model to everyone on November 12.

facts.text: API price per generated view: $0.04 for the first frame and $0.008 per subsequent frame at 720p; refined splats cost $5.
facts.quote: Generating a view costs $0.04 for the first frame and $0.008 for each subsequent frame at 720p (the highest resolution that the API offers). Turning views into refined splats is priced at $5.

facts.text: Users get $10 of free API credits and a separate $10 for the web apps.
facts.quote: Users receive $10 of free API credits and a separate $10 for the web apps to get started.

stories.headline: AMD closes its all-stock acquisition of World Labs, valued at about $8.2 billion
stories.quote: In September 2026, AMD agreed to acquire World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at about $8.2 billion. The deal closed on November 16, and the company named Li AMD’s chief scientist and executive vice president.
stories.description: Builds world models that generate 3D scenes and camera-controllable video

facts.text: AMD agreed to the all-stock deal, valued at about $8.2 billion, in September 2026.
facts.quote: In September 2026, AMD agreed to acquire World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at about $8.2 billion.

facts.text: The deal closed on November 16; co-founder Fei-Fei Li was named AMD's chief scientist and executive vice president.
facts.quote: The deal closed on November 16, and the company named Li AMD’s chief scientist and executive vice president.

facts.text: Neither AMD statement mentions Atlas or the future of World Labs' products.
facts.quote: Neither AMD’s initial announcement nor its closing statement mentions Atlas or says what will happen to World Labs’ products.

stories.headline: Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face cited as background
stories.quote: Nvidia under Huang was among the biggest boosters of open weight AI models, whether through its own Nemotron series, its acquisition of Hugging Face, or support for models outside its own ecosystem.
